description: Hello, my name is Maryam and I’m an avid astrophysics and space enthusiast. This is my first time participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge and I look forward to collaborating with my teammates and gaining valuable knowledge along this journey.
summary:
Notable Space agencies such as NASA and SpaceX are preparing to send more missions to Mars, with SpaceX planning to send uncrewed cargo missions by 2028 and NASA planning to send humans by late 2030’s.
These missions require a steady source of propulsion fuel hence our team came up with the idea of utilising the hydrogen reserves and atmospheric carbon dioxide on mars to produce rocket fuel and facilitate interplanetary travel.
With reference to the Sabatier reaction, hydrogen extracted from the ice and carbon dioxide present on Mars will be used to synthesize Methane for rocket fuel. Hence, we created a map highlighting the main areas where these raw materials are abundantly present and where potential methane synthesis outposts could be constructed. Not only will this make missions to Mars cheaper by reducing rocket launch mass, these outposts can readily sustain self-sufficient energy production for future Martian colonies.
Our team built a website showing a detailed map of mars with properties similar to google maps. You can switch through different layers that represent data relevant to the issue we are addressing. The map has a live update function and is incorporated with distance calculation algorithms which means you can check how far away points on the map are from each other. A side panel displays traversal distance, coordinates of the outposts as well as rover transit time.
details:
Our team built a website showing a detailed map of mars with properties similar to google maps. You can switch through different layers that represent data relevant to the issue we are addressing. The map has a live update function and is incorporated with distance calculation algorithms which means you can check how far away points on the map are from each other. You can also pinpoint exact locations on the map and can create an entire trail you'd like to take through the Martian surface. A side panel displays traversal distance, coordinates of the outposts as well as rover transit time.  

This map can be used by scientists and researchers to mark points where there is an abundance of raw material to set up methane synthesis outposts.

We decided to use the NASA mars trek website to create our main base map. We integrated the Mars trek API directly through leaflet–our mapping library– to create a live update function and handle distance calculation algorithms. We used HTML for the structure of the website, CSS for the stylistic execution and JavaScript for making the website functional. Most of the coding was carried out independently but we did utilise the Gemini SI to refine the code to ensure the website worked smoothly.

Our project incorporates multiple Martian maps showcasing different properties in one website, which we don't think is easily accessible anywhere else. Since we are also avid supporters of open science our website is free to be availed by the public. Moreover, one unique aspect that we all find useful is that when we mark a point on the map, we can type out corresponding notes, making it easier to store and sort information.

However, the team agrees that there wasn't an extensive repository of data available to incorporate the level of detail we would've preferred, and this might be a weakness of our project. Nonetheless, we all believe that this project surely developed our skills and helped us learn new ones.
